The writer pressing a few banknotes into the trader’s hand; wedding garlands and lamps in the background, partly taken down. Characters (keep them identical on every slide): The narrator: a Bengali writer in his forties, white dhoti and shawl, round spectacles, gentle face. Mini: a five-year-old girl with a short bob and a red-bordered frock (later a quiet young woman, then a bride in red Benarasi silk with sandal-paste marks). Mini’s mother: slim, in a plain cotton sari with a red border, anxious eyes. Rahmat: a tall, broad Afghan fruit seller in a loose pale tunic and baggy trousers, a brown waistcoat, a wound turban, a short dark beard, a heavy cloth bag on his shoulder (thinner and greyer after prison). Warm hand-painted gouache and coloured pencil, lightly textured paper, sophisticated storybook illustration with believable Bengali environments, expressive natural faces and coherent scale. Forest teal, terracotta, saffron and cream palette. Full-bleed landscape 3:2 composition. NO text, lettering, numerals, speech bubbles, border, logos, emoji or watermarks. One complete scene, not a collage or contact sheet.
